question: To whom is this vision of Obadiah addressed, and with what images does the prophet describe the security Edom trusted in?
Why does the text call Jacob “your brother,” and what does the memory of the story of Esau and Jacob add to the accusations against Edom?

The word יוֹם (yom, “day”) is repeated many times in verses 11 to 14 and returns in the “day of the LORD”: how does the prophet link the day of Judah's calamity to the day that will come upon the nations?
How does the principle “as you have done, it will be done to you” relate to the final promise that “the kingdom will belong to the LORD”?
The text condemns whoever looked “with gloating” on a brother's misfortune: how do you react inside when someone you dislike goes through hardship?
